source.title: H-GAP: Humanoid Control with a Generalist Planner
source.authors: Zhengyao Jiang; Ying-Chen Xu; Nolan Wagener; Yi-Chen Luo; Michael Janner; Edward Grefenstette; Tim Rocktäschel; Yuan-Dong Tian

record.tranche_reason: Studies model- and dataset-scaling in humanoid trajectory generation, a different setting from language-model scaling, but does not test the specific power-law, extrapolation, or compute-allocation claims.
record.gate_note: The paper reports scaling results for H-GAP, but does not fit power laws or test held-out language-model cross-entropy, extrapolation from small runs, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. It cites prior scaling work as motivation. The reported humanoid-model results are recorded as related findings, not as tests of the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study trains H-GAP humanoid trajectory models from 6M to 300M parameters on MoCapAct subsets of 10–100%, but reports only qualitative trends read from figures. It fits no power law, reports no exponents, and runs no extrapolation, fixed-compute allocation or fixed-parameter shape comparison. It does not study language models. Kaplan, Henighan and Hoffmann are cited only as motivation. The monotone validation-loss decrease with size (Fig. 3b) cannot show whether a power-law form holds, so it cannot test V5. Downstream-control results concern a non-language planner, so they fall outside V6's language-model scope. All findings are recorded as fits_no_version. The reader's T3 overstates the link, since there is no result on any claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find that larger models improve validation loss and imitation but not downstream control, which they describe as mixed or degrading and call 'model scaling saturation'. Larger and more diverse data improves both imitation and downstream control. The abstract summarises this as gains possible 'via additional data but not computing'.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales a humanoid state-action trajectory model and dataset, measuring validation loss, state-prediction error, imitation, and control performance. It does not use language-model held-out cross-entropy, fit the claimed loss power laws, extrapolate from small runs, or find a compute-optimal parameter/token split.
record.method_sensitivity: The largest model's training curves were unusual; the authors note learning rate as a possible factor and report that a smaller rate has been found to accelerate learning of larger models. Dataset size and diversity affect imitation and downstream performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 6M–300M H-GAP models, validation loss and imitation returns improve with size, but downstream MPC control returns do not improve and are described as degrading. Latent-code entropy falls with size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In planning-based humanoid control, lower self-supervised loss from model scaling need not translate to better downstream control, possibly because generation diversity falls.

fits_no_version.finding: With 40M models, more MoCapAct data (10% to 100%, 7M to 67M transitions) improves both imitation and downstream returns.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For humanoid trajectory models, data scaling improves downstream control where model scaling saturates.

fits_no_version.finding: State-prediction MSE improves only marginally with size (about 0.07 to 0.06). The 300M model shows unusual training curves, which the authors attribute possibly to the learning rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model-size gains in humanoid dynamics prediction are small and sensitive to optimisation settings.

record.problems: No power-law fits, exponents, or compute-optimal allocation results are reported. Scaling outcomes are mostly described qualitatively from figures; individual plotted scaling values are not stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported scaling result was left out.

untested.parts: No language models; no power-law fit of loss in parameters, data or compute.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count; depth and width co-vary with size in Table 5.
Loss is reported across sizes in a non-text modality, but no power-law form is fitted or checked, and data scaling reports returns, not loss.
No language-model downstream predictability. The humanoid downstream control results are outside the version's scope.
No exponents or fitting choices are compared.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T3 was changed to T6/discusses because no claim version is tested. Results are figure-read and qualitative, with no numeric scaling values in the text except the state-prediction MSE bars in Fig. 3d. In Table 5, depth, width and training steps all vary with model size; the 300M model trains for 1e8 steps versus 5e7 for the others, which confounds size comparisons.

versions.untested_parts: No language models or held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy are tested.
No predictions from small-run power-law fits are compared with larger runs.
No fixed-compute parameter/token allocation sweep or compute-optimal split is tested.
No architecture-shape comparison at fixed parameter count is reported.
The study scales a humanoid trajectory model and dataset, but does not test whether a power-law form holds in this or another modality or training regime.
Downstream humanoid-control results are reported, but their predictability from language-model scale or pretraining loss is not tested.
No fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocations are compared across fitting choices or setups.

rows.subject: H-GAP
rows.operation_detail: Compared model sizes and reported training and validation loss trends.
rows.value: Validation-set accuracy improves with larger models; the paper notes a substantial improvement from 100M to 300M.
rows.note: The result is described qualitatively; no power-law fit or exponent is reported.
rows.check: Value says 'validation-set accuracy'. The plotted measure is validation loss of the latent-code prior (Fig. 3b), which falls with size and drops notably from 100M to 300M. Per Appendix B, the 300M curves are unusual, which may confound the 100M-to-300M jump. The measure is not language-model held-out loss and has no fitted form, so it links to no version.

rows.subject: H-GAP
rows.operation_detail: Compared imitation-task performance across model sizes.
rows.value: Larger models significantly improve imitation performance.
rows.uncertainty: Standard errors are reported for imitation experiments over 30 seeds; individual plotted values are not stated in the text.
rows.note: The reported result is a qualitative trend across the tested model sizes.

rows.subject: H-GAP
rows.operation_detail: Compared downstream control performance across model sizes.
rows.value: Larger models do not consistently outperform smaller models; the paper also describes downstream performance as degrading as model size scales.
rows.uncertainty: Standard errors are reported for downstream experiments over 300 seeds; individual plotted values are not stated in the text.
rows.note: The paper attributes the mixed or degrading result to reduced generation diversity and steerability.
rows.check: Linking to none is correct. The text does more than say results are mixed: it says 'we observe degrading performance on downstream control tasks as model size scales'. The value should state that degradation explicitly, since 'partial' undersells it.

rows.subject: H-GAP
rows.operation_detail: Compared entropy of generated latent codes across model sizes.
rows.measure: Average entropy of generated latent codes
rows.value: Larger models generally produce latent codes with lower entropy.
rows.note: The authors interpret lower entropy as reduced diversity in generated control signals.

rows.subject: H-GAP
rows.operation_detail: Compared state-prediction accuracy across H-GAP sizes and against TAP.
rows.baseline: TAP is included as a comparison; no numerical baseline is stated in the text.
rows.value: Larger H-GAP models only marginally improve prediction accuracy.
rows.note: The paper compares sampled model trajectories with simulator rollouts using the same actions.

rows.subject: H-GAP 300M
rows.operation_detail: Reported training curves for the largest model.
rows.value: The authors observed unusual training curves for the largest model.
rows.note: The authors suggest the learning rate may contribute and note that a smaller learning rate has been found to accelerate learning of larger models.
